building.name: San Francisco Gas Light Company Headquarters

historical_record.description: The San Francisco Gas Light Company put up its headquarters here in 1893, alongside two large gas holding tanks that stood until the Marina was built out. The tanks are gone; the office building is San Francisco City Landmark No. 58.
Robert Durden photographed the property, showing San Francisco Gas Light Company.

historic_survey.note: From the survey's appendix table of unreinforced masonry buildings and their historic ratings, study area 11 (Outlying).

historic_survey.survey: Victorian Era Styles Historic Context Statement (2022)
historic_survey.note: One of the few known Richardsonian Romanesque buildings in the city, judged individually significant for its round tower with a conical roof, corbelled cornice, arched window surrounds and Syrian arch at the entry — a two-storey brick industrial building, now in commercial use.
